title: DDR4 PHY Receiver Front-End
short: Channel modelling and a source-degenerated CTLE for a 1.6 Gbps receiver in TSMC 65 nm CMOS.
where: Department of Electrical Engineering, IIT Bombay
summary: The goal is a receiver front-end for a DDR4-class link at 1.6 Gbps (unit interval 625 ps, Nyquist frequency 800 MHz) in TSMC 65 nm CMOS with a 1.2 V supply. The channel is modelled with a physical multi-conductor transmission line (Cadence mtline, FieldSolver wideband model) instead of ideal RLC sections, and ideal resistors and capacitors are replaced by the process's rnpoly resistors and MIM capacitors.

The first result concerns the channel itself. Loss at the Nyquist frequency grows with trace length and is very small for realistic DDR4 traces: below 0.02 dB at 2.5 cm, 0.08 dB at 10 cm and 1.2 dB at 90 cm. Significant loss needs either a much higher data rate or a much longer channel, so the amount of equalization a link needs is set jointly by length and data rate.

To study equalization where it matters, I used an intentionally long 8 m line, which rolls off by 8.09 dB between DC and 800 MHz. A source-degenerated CTLE (differential pair with an R<sub>S</sub>–C<sub>S</sub> degeneration network) designed for 8.87 dB of peaking at 800 MHz flattens this response to within 0.77 dB, raises the eye SNR from 8.39 dB to 18.45 dB and cuts peak-to-peak jitter by 69%. At the 2.5 cm trace the channel is nearly flat, so the CTLE is not needed for loss there; it stays in the chain for signal conditioning, common-mode rejection and isolation of the channel from the comparator.

title: First-Principles Study of Monolayer 2H-MoS₂
short: DFT-PBE study of monolayer MoS₂: structure, elasticity, bands, phonons and spin–orbit coupling.
where: Laboratoire des Solides Irradiés (LSI), École Polytechnique, Institut Polytechnique de Paris
summary: A first-principles characterisation of monolayer 2H-MoS₂ with density-functional theory (PBE) in Quantum ESPRESSO, covering its structural, elastic, electronic, vibrational and spin–orbit properties. Each computed quantity is checked against the others and against published values.

The elastic constants give a layer incompressibility modulus of about 84 N/m, within roughly 1% of the literature, which validates the computational setup. The band structure has a direct gap of about 1.68 eV at K, and the phonon dispersion has real frequencies across the whole Brillouin zone, so the structure is dynamically stable at equilibrium. Spin–orbit coupling splits the K-valley valence band by 148 meV, and a maximally-localised Wannier function model reproduces the bands with a few meV of RMS interpolation error.

title: NUS Young Fellowship Programme
short: Selected for the 2025 programme at the National University of Singapore.
where: NUS Graduate School and SCALE, National University of Singapore
summary: Selected for the 2025 NUS Young Fellowship Programme. The programme included mentored research tutorials, meetings with faculty and visits to laboratories in Singapore. I presented a research poster and an oral talk, took part in the 3-Minute Thesis (3MT) challenge, and met a cohort from many disciplines who were considering research and doctoral study.
